summary: Increase the Inquisition's ordinary Conviction generation from a heavily contested Aftermath and improve the efficiency of the 1-Conviction Discard-Pile Purge so Purification becomes a more credible alternate victory path.

conviction.trigger: The first qualifying Aftermath each turn in which one or more opposing cards enter the Graveyard.
conviction.note: The increased gain is capped at 2 for the qualifying Aftermath. It is not 1 Conviction per card, so mass-Graveyard effects do not independently fill the tracker beyond this +2 normal gain.

unchanged: Conviction begins at 0 and has a maximum of 4.
Condemnation continues to send opposing Tactics to the Graveyard during Aftermath.
Blasphemy remains a separate +1 Conviction source for qualifying opposing Arcane plays and reveals.
Purification still requires the opponent's normal start-of-turn draw to fail because both Draw Pile and Discard Pile are empty.
Grand Inquisitor Final Judgment and Witch Hunter Relentless Pursuit are otherwise unchanged.
evaluationGoal: Test whether Purification becomes a meaningful late-game threat before ordinary battlefield victory is effectively decided, without making Inquisition combat power or resource generation excessive.
